subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be driven by live gateway runtime truth, by a passive plugin status API, or by the current local `not checked` plus opt-in local-probe split?
rationale: Current main only partially mitigates the old misleading wording, while the broader open issue and the conflicting fork PR leave the permanent status boundary unresolved.

options.title: Use live gateway truth
options.body: Make the broader live-gateway status contract canonical, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Define passive plugin status
options.body: Keep status read-only by adding or documenting a passive memory-plugin status contract instead of probing heavyweight runtime managers locally.

options.title: Accept the current split
options.body: Declare `not checked` sufficient for skipped memory inspection and close the competing implementation paths without claiming live runtime health.

recommendation.title: Use live gateway truth
recommendation.body: Make the broader live-gateway status contract canonical, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The central status and memory-runtime history points to steipete as the strongest owner for choosing the long-term status boundary.
